description: Make terminal text bigger or smaller, and pick the font it is drawn in, on this device only: a phone and a big screen can each keep their own. Every open terminal changes at once, with no reload. Prompt-theme icons (starship, powerlevel10k) draw through a bundled icon font whatever font you pick. Bigger text in one window can shrink a session you also have open in another window, because a shared pane takes the smallest window's size; the size crown decides which window sets it.
examples: On a 4K screen, press Ctrl+Cmd+= twice and every terminal is two points bigger.
On the phone, open Settings, terminal and set the size to 11 so more of Claude's output fits.
Type JetBrains Mono as the font and the terminals switch to it; clear the box to go back to the system font.
how_to: Press Ctrl+Cmd+= for bigger text, Ctrl+Cmd+- for smaller, Ctrl+Cmd+0 for the default size.
Or open Settings, terminal, text: use a- and a+ (9 to 28), or reset.
Type a font name in the font box (the desktop app can list your installed fonts) and leave the box to apply it; the preview line shows it first.
media_exempt: recaptured at the version bump with the other settings screens
name: Terminal text size and font
summary: Change terminal text size and font per device from Settings, terminal, or with Ctrl+Cmd+= / - / 0.
where: Ctrl+Cmd+= / Ctrl+Cmd+- / Ctrl+Cmd+0 from anywhere in the app.
